original_question: Characterize those Scott well-filtered dcpos P for which, for every Scott well-filtered dcpo Q, the product P x Q is again Scott well-filtered.
target_in_paper: Section 4, Question 4.9: "Characterize those Scott well-filtered dcpos P for which the products P × Q is Scott well-filtered for every Scott well-filtered dcpo Q."
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper's official formulation. It correctly identifies the target class as Scott well-filtered dcpos, asks for a characterization of those P with a universal product-preservation property, and quantifies over every Scott well-filtered dcpo Q. It therefore matches Question 4.9, not the neighboring yes/no product question in Question 4.7.
missing_details: Make explicit that "Scott well-filtered" means: for a dcpo R, its Scott space ΣR = (R, σ(R)) is well-filtered.
Specify that P × Q is the product dcpo, equipped with the coordinatewise order.
Clarify that the conclusion is about the Scott space Σ(P × Q), not merely about the ordinary topological product ΣP × ΣQ.

If full self-containment is desired, unpack "well-filtered": a T0 space X is well-filtered if for every open set U and every filtered family 𝒦 of compact saturated subsets of X, from ⋂𝒦 ⊆ U it follows that K ⊆ U for some K in 𝒦.
State explicitly that no additional hypotheses such as continuity, sobriety, core compactness, or domain structure are assumed beyond P and Q being dcpos with the stated Scott well-filteredness.
refined_question: Characterize the dcpos P such that ΣP = (P, σ(P)) is well-filtered and, for every dcpo Q whose Scott space ΣQ = (Q, σ(Q)) is well-filtered, the Scott space Σ(P × Q) of the coordinatewise product dcpo P × Q is well-filtered; here a T0 space X is well-filtered if, whenever U is open and 𝒦 is a filtered family of compact saturated subsets of X with ⋂𝒦 ⊆ U, some K ∈ 𝒦 satisfies K ⊆ U.
justification: The draft matches the paper's official Question 4.9 almost verbatim in Section 4. Definition 4.4 on the same page fixes the terminology "Scott well-filtered" as meaning exactly that the Scott space ΣP is well-filtered. Section 2 supplies the notation ΣP = (P, σ(P)) and the paper's definition of well-filtered spaces. The only real sharpening needed is to make the product structure explicit: the intended object is the Scott space of the product dcpo P × Q, not just the topological product of Scott spaces. This is therefore the precise paper-faithful target, rather than the neighboring yes/no product problem in Question 4.7.
